answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral, so coordinated equivocation by k identities triggers aggregate penalties proportional to k², not k independent fixed fines. Detection also compounds asymmetric depreciation across seized escrows, making a controlled swarm incur an exponential multiplier in capital loss. Like an island exposed to a gale beneath a nebula, no identity can safely hide in the crowd: shared evidence links coordinated proofs and raises the cost of splitting stake.
